summary: Lean weekly run over 30 screenshots and 10 bot reports. The good news is that the desktop scan flow reads clearly and the core counting path looks sound. The serious news is security: the run surfaced 3 blockers and 21 high findings, led by tenant and access exposure (an auth-bypass flag, a client-supplied businessId, and role gating that only hides data in the UI while the raw codes still sit in the browser store for every role). Mobile is the other weak spot, where the scan feedback is buried below the session controls and the input is not auto-focused. Fix the security and tenant items first, then the mobile scan layout. Decode accuracy is provisional because the 10 ground-truth codes are not confirmed yet.

priorities.title: Rotate the leaked Anthropic and SerpAPI keys NOW, then stop test reports from saving your secrets to git
Lock down the AI lookup endpoint: today anyone can hit it and run up your Gemini/OpenAI bill with no login and no real spending limit
Fix the phone view: the scan box and the last-scan confirmation are buried below the fold, so a counter on a phone cannot see if a scan worked
Build real role-based data protection on the server before selling to a second shop: right now every employee's browser downloads the full product/code database
Clean up customer-facing wording (drop 'AI lookup', 'Gemini', 'OpenAI', 'alias') and auto-focus the scan box, and fix the 'Saved: 0 while Synced' counter that looks broken in a demo

findings.title: Desktop scan page communicates purpose clearly in under 10 seconds
findings.recommendation: No change needed here. The scan box, Ready to scan label, live feed, and counts table all read correctly at a glance.

findings.title: Phone view: session controls bury the scan feedback below the fold
findings.recommendation: Collapse the session / export / import controls into a single disclosure row or move them below the live feed. The scan input and the last-scan confirmation row must both be visible without scrolling at 390px width.

findings.title: Internal terms leak into user-facing copy: AI lookup, approved alias, provider names
findings.recommendation: Replace 'AI lookup' with 'Auto-identify unknown items', replace 'approved alias' in the Reason column with 'Recognized barcode', and rename 'Needs Review' to something like 'Unrecognized items' or 'Items to sort'. Remove provider names (Gemini, OpenAI) from any customer-visible screen.

findings.title: Scan input requires a manual click to focus; not auto-focused on page load
findings.recommendation: Auto-focus the scan input on page load so a scanner gun fires immediately without a click. The placeholder already says 'Click here, then scan' which confirms the click requirement. Remove that barrier.

findings.title: Phone view scan feed table truncates columns; Status and Saved columns disappear off-screen
findings.recommendation: On mobile, collapse the feed table to show only Product, Qty, and a status icon. Full columns belong behind a row-tap detail view or a horizontal scroll with sticky first column.

findings.title: Scan input placeholder says 'Click here' but the field is already auto-focused
evidence: src/components/ScannerInput.tsx:134 placeholder='Click here, then scan or type a code and press Enter'
reports/agent-bots/latest/ux_scorecard.md: 'Find where to scan' FAIL, friction=1, note='scan input is the focused default'
findings.recommendation: Change the placeholder to 'Scan a code or type and press Enter' (no 'Click here' since focus is automatic). The UX bot rated this friction=1 but it is still a real discoverability gap for new users who do not realize the field already has focus.

findings.title: Counts table lacks a 'Correct' button - human correction flow may be absent or renamed
evidence: playwright-results.json: CustomerReadableControlsBot failed at customer-readable-controls.spec.ts:32 - getByTestId('final-count-body').getByRole('button', { name: 'Correct' }) not found
findings.recommendation: Verify whether the 'Correct' correction action on a count row was removed, renamed, or never implemented. If it was renamed (e.g., to 'Modify'), update the bot spec. If the human-correction flow for disputed counts was intentionally removed, document the decision and ensure there is still a path to correct an over- or under-counted row without doing a full delete+rescan.

findings.title: Needs Review reason text is truncated in the data_integrity_report.md table
evidence: reports/agent-bots/latest/data_integrity_report.md row for unknown code 999000111222 - reason cell cut off at 'searched the barcode databases and t'
findings.recommendation: The truncation is a cosmetic report artifact, not a runtime issue. The screenshot (02-unknown.png) confirms the full reason is displayed in the UI. No code change required; widen the markdown table column or use a separate detail block if the full reason text matters for audit trails.

findings.title: Role gating is UI-only: full NeedsReview/scan data (raw codes, provider names, decode traces) is in the Zustand store for all roles; only JSX conditionals hide it
findings.recommendation: Strip sensitive fields from the store state slice exposed to non-platform users, not only from JSX render output. The current localStorage partialize (scanPersist.ts) does strip on write, but in-memory the full payload remains accessible via browser devtools or a React renderer. For the customer role, filter the needsReviewQueue and scanFeed arrays before they enter the Zustand state subscribers, or ensure the resolved-scan API route returns only CUSTOMER_SAFE_* shapes so raw codes never reach the client bundle at all.

findings.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEN_ACCESS=1 bypasses the entire AuthGuard with no server-side enforcement
findings.recommendation: Remove or harden the OPEN_ACCESS flag before any multi-tenant or production deployment. If a demo mode is needed, add a server-side read-only mock backend check so setting the flag cannot expose real business data. At minimum, document in RISK_REGISTER.md that this flag must never be set in any deployment that holds real inventory data, and add a build-time check that blocks deployment when NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEN_ACCESS=1 and NODE_ENV=production.

findings.title: resolve-scan route accepts businessId from the request body; a malicious client could pass another business's ID if Firebase member check is absent or misconfigured
findings.recommendation: In the Firestore-backed path, verify that the authenticated uid is a member of the requested businessId before querying that business's products and aliases (the code does call memberDocId check at line 77, but the fallback when Firebase is unavailable or emulator mode is active should be explicitly audited). Add an integration test that proves a uid not in business-A cannot resolve against business-A's data, even by spoofing the businessId field.

findings.title: Sanitizer only masks cost/price when a labeled keyword is present; an unlabeled bare dollar amount (e.g. a price in a product notes field) passes through to AI
findings.recommendation: Consider masking all bare $X.XX patterns regardless of context, or document the design decision that notes fields are trusted to not contain standalone prices. Add a sanitizer test case for an unlabeled dollar amount to confirm current behavior is intentional.

findings.title: AI confidence percentage is visible to all roles in the Needs Review table, not gated behind isPlatform
findings.recommendation: Decide whether confidence is a customer-facing field. If it reveals internal AI scoring that should be manager/platformOwner-only, wrap the confidence cell in the isPlatform guard. If it is acceptable for customers to see a confidence indicator, document this as an intentional disclosure.

findings.title: No .env.example file found in the repository root
findings.recommendation: Add a .env.example listing all required variable names (GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS, FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*, etc.) with placeholder values only. This prevents accidental real-key commits and serves as onboarding documentation.

findings.title: verifiedFacts and guesses rendered in NeedsReviewTable without isPlatform guard
findings.businessImpact: Customer-side users see internal AI reasoning strings (verifiedFacts, guesses) that are meant to be platformOwner diagnostics only. These are in-session memory only - not persisted to localStorage - but any customer with an open Needs Review item sees them live.
findings.securityImpact: Leaks internal AI decode reasoning to customer-side roles. verifiedFacts is explicitly listed in SENSITIVE_FIELDS (sensitiveFields.ts:13). guesses is an internal AI field not in SENSITIVE_FIELDS but also not in CUSTOMER_SAFE_REVIEW_FIELDS. Both render unconditionally.
findings.explanation: Lines 186-191 of NeedsReviewTable.tsx render review.verifiedFacts and review.guesses with no isPlatform check. All other sensitive decode internals on that page (evidenceStrength, crossCheckDecision, decodeProviderSummaries, sourceUrls, rawCode, cleanCode, providerName) are correctly wrapped in isPlatform guards. These two fields were missed. The localStorage serializer (scanPersist.ts) strips them on persist, so the leak is session-memory-only, not disk.
findings.fix: Add isPlatform guard around the verifiedFacts and guesses spans, matching the pattern used for sourceUrls at line 192. Also add verifiedFacts and guesses to SENSITIVE_FIELDS and/or exclude them explicitly from CUSTOMER_SAFE_REVIEW_FIELDS (guesses is already absent; add explicit comment).

findings.title: confidence and autoVerifyScore shown to all roles in NeedsReviewTable
findings.businessImpact: Customer users see a numeric decode confidence percentage and the autoVerifyScore diagnostic in the Needs Review table. The comment in sensitiveFields.ts line 50 explicitly names confidence as an internal field excluded from CUSTOMER_SAFE_REVIEW_FIELDS, but neither is in the SENSITIVE_FIELDS denylist array, and both render unconditionally.
findings.securityImpact: Exposes AI confidence scores to customer roles. This reveals internal model quality signals, which the design treats as platformOwner-only diagnostics. Low severity because it does not expose raw codes, aliases, or provider names - but it contradicts the stated design.
findings.explanation: NeedsReviewTable.tsx line 207 renders review.confidence as a percentage for every role. Line 150-153 renders review.autoVerifyScore also without isPlatform guard. The sensitiveFields.ts comment at line 50 lists confidence in the exclusion rationale, but confidence is not in the SENSITIVE_FIELDS array, so the generic stripSensitive() defense-in-depth stripping does not catch it. Neither field is in CUSTOMER_SAFE_REVIEW_FIELDS.
findings.fix: Either add isPlatform guards to the confidence and autoVerifyScore display cells, or add confidence and autoVerifyScore to SENSITIVE_FIELDS so the stripSensitive defense catches them everywhere. The Needs Review table header already hides the Provider column with isPlatform; apply the same pattern to the Confidence column header and cell.

findings.title: Role gating is client-side only - auth-bypass user sees full platformOwner view
findings.businessImpact: The client-side isPlatformOwner flag controls what is rendered. When the E2E auth-bypass is active (NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS=1 in Playwright specs), effectiveClientAccessLevel returns platform unconditionally (NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_PLATFORM_OWNER=1 in playwright.config.ts), so all 11 mock E2E specs exercise the full platformOwner view. The auth-bypass is correctly blocked in NODE_ENV=production, so this is a test-only exposure, not a production bypass. However, real production customer-side role enforcement (the businessOwner/admin/counter/viewer gates) is still entirely DEFERRED per HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md. Until a real signed-in business user exists, there is no live proof that the gates work for non-mock users.
findings.securityImpact: In production with Firebase Auth active, the NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS/UIDS lists gate the client-side isPlatformOwner. If those env vars are empty or misconfigured, every authenticated user gets the business (customer) view - acceptable. The risk is the opposite misconfiguration: if NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS is too broad, customer users could be promoted to the platformOwner view client-side. Server-side data access (the /api/resolve-scan endpoint) uses PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS/UIDS (server-only, never public), which is correct and independent.
findings.explanation: Role gating is intentionally deferred (HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md). The client-side only check means the Products page, NeedsReviewTable, and LiveScanFeed all rely on isPlatformOwner() from a client env-var check. There is no server enforcement of which UI fields are rendered. The server endpoint (/api/resolve-scan) does enforce the data shape server-side correctly. The gap is the in-session Zustand store: when a customer loads the app in mock/dev mode with no real auth, userId is null, effectiveClientAccessLevel returns business (customer), so the store holds the full platformOwner data in memory but the UI only renders the customer-safe columns. A user who can read Zustand state (browser devtools) sees everything regardless.
findings.fix: This is the deferred foundation per HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md. Priority: implement server-side customer resolution so the Zustand store never holds the alias/catalog DB for customer sessions. The auth-bypass test concern is already correctly guarded (NODE_ENV=production check).

findings.title: catalogEntries collection is globally readable by any signed-in user
findings.businessImpact: Any signed-in user can read the global catalogEntries collection directly from the client. This collection contains normalizedBarcode values (the global barcode-to-product catalog). A customer-side user can enumerate the global catalog by querying catalogEntries, extracting all normalizedBarcode values. This is the global code database that customer roles are explicitly prohibited from downloading per HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md.
findings.securityImpact: Allows any authenticated customer to enumerate the raw global barcode catalog from Firestore directly (not through the sanitized server endpoint). The Firestore rule intentionally allows reads ('any signed-in user reads') for performance reasons, but this contradicts the design requirement that the full alias/catalog DB must never be downloadable by customers. Client writes are correctly blocked.
findings.explanation: The test at tenantIsolation.rules.test.ts:112 asserts assertSucceeds for User B reading catalogEntries. HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md explicitly states full alias/catalog/index download = platformOwner-only. The catalogEntries rule grants read to all authenticated users as a deliberate design choice for local resolution speed, but this conflicts with the stated data-protection design. Once real customer roles are live, any signed-in shop user can getDocs(collection(db, 'catalogEntries')) to dump the global catalog.
findings.fix: Either (a) enforce the server-side customer resolution path so customers never query Firestore directly (they call /api/resolve-scan instead, which shapes the response), or (b) restrict catalogEntries reads to platformOwner via custom claims or a server-only path. The simpler near-term fix: document this as a known deferred item with a TODO in the Firestore rules and ensure the deferred server-side customer resolution (HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md) is implemented before any non-platformOwner user accesses the live Firestore project.

findings.title: exportFinalCounts and exportProducts contain raw barcode/GTIN/UPC/EAN and alias fields - no call-site role check outside ExportMenu
findings.businessImpact: The raw platformOwner export functions (exportFinalCounts, exportProducts, exportAliases, exportRawScanLog) include primaryBarcode, gtin, upc, ean, aliases, raw_code, clean_code, normalized_candidates, providerName, confidence. These functions are correctly NOT offered in the ExportMenu for business roles. However, they are exported from csvExport.ts with no guard on the function itself - any future call site that forgets the role check would expose them. The customer-safe variants (exportFinalCountsCustomer, etc.) exist and are used correctly in ExportMenu.
findings.securityImpact: Current state: the ExportMenu correctly routes business roles to sanitized export functions. The risk is future call-site drift - the unguarded raw functions are importable by any component. There is no defense-in-depth at the function level (unlike the serializers which accept an AccessLevel parameter). If a new page or component calls exportFinalCounts() without checking the role, it silently leaks all barcode data.
findings.explanation: ExportMenu.tsx correctly uses isPlatform to decide which export functions to call (lines 53-77). The sanitized customer exports have no code-bearing fields. But exportFinalCounts, exportProducts, exportAliases, exportRawScanLog are standalone functions with no AccessLevel parameter - they always produce the raw format. Any future component that bypasses ExportMenu would expose raw codes without warning.
findings.fix: Add an AccessLevel parameter to the raw export functions (or a single exportForRole wrapper) so the correct sanitized variant is always selected at the function level. This mirrors the serializer pattern in serializers.ts. Low urgency while ExportMenu is the only call site, but important before the role model is expanded.

findings.title: platformOwner can inspect and repair global data safely (legitimate path confirmed intact)
findings.businessImpact: No blockage. The platformOwner path works correctly: server-side isPlatformOwnerServer() uses PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS/UIDS (non-public env), the /api/resolve-scan endpoint skips the membership check for platform level and returns the full internal result, the Products page shows all code columns, and the ExportMenu offers all raw exports including aliases and raw scan log.
findings.securityImpact: No issue. The legitimate platformOwner repair path is functional and server-enforced for the API endpoint. Client-side gating provides the UI view.
findings.explanation: platformOwner detection uses two independent allowlists: server-side (PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAILS/UIDS, read from non-public env in API routes) and client-side (NEXT_PUBLIC_PLATFORM_OWNER_*, used only for UI rendering). The server-side check in /api/resolve-scan correctly bypasses the business membership requirement for platform users and returns the full unredacted result. The Products page, ExportMenu, NeedsReviewTable, and LiveScanFeed all render full debug detail when isPlatform is true.
findings.fix: No fix needed. Status note: the server-side repair path requires FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_PATH to be configured for live cloud use - documented in route.ts comments as an ops step.

findings.title: Anthropic API key and SerpAPI key committed to git history in Playwright results file
findings.affects: all consumers of this repo; key owner (djsanti88@gmail.com)
evidence: Key appears in 3 committed shas: f65c082, a11d265, e5c2e16

Root cause: playwright.bots.config.ts line 32: env: { ...process.env, IS_E2E: '1', ... } spreads the entire OS environment into the Playwright webServer config, and Playwright records the full env block in the JSON reporter output
findings.businessImpact: Live Anthropic API key is exposed; any party with repo access (or who ever cloned it) can burn paid API credits. SerpAPI key similarly exposed. Keys must be rotated immediately.
findings.securityImpact: Credential exposure in version control history. Keys remain exploitable from any point in history even after a file update unless history is scrubbed.
findings.explanation: The Playwright bot config spreads the full process environment into the webServer env block. Playwright's JSON reporter faithfully serializes that entire env map into reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json. That file is tracked by git (not in .gitignore) and was committed three times with the live key present. The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is a Claude Code shell variable (not an app variable), but it is present in the process environment when qa:bots runs and therefore gets captured.
findings.fix: 1. Rotate ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and SERPAPI_KEY immediately. 2. In playwright.bots.config.ts replace '...process.env' with an explicit allowlist of only the env vars the app actually needs (IS_E2E, NEXT_PUBLIC_*, app-specific AI keys). 3. Add reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json to .gitignore. 4. Scrub git history (git filter-repo or BFG) to remove the committed secret. 5. Add a pre-commit hook or CI check (e.g. gitleaks) to block future secret commits.

findings.title: POST /api/ai-lookup has no authentication, no server-side rate limit, and no server-side daily spend cap
findings.affects: owner's Gemini and OpenAI API budgets; any unauthenticated caller
evidence: autocannon -d 8 -c 50 http://localhost:3000/api/ai-lookup: 3,318 requests in 8.03s, 0 non-2xx, 0 errors, avg latency 139ms
GET /api/ai-lookup returns 200 with no auth header/cookie required
grep for 'rateLimit|rateLimiter|throttle|429' in src/app/api/ai-lookup/route.ts: no matches
grep for 'dailyCount|dailyLimit|daily_cap|DAILY' in route.ts: only 'dailyLimit: Number(process.env.AI_LOOKUP_DAILY_LIMIT || 200)' returned in GET config payload; no server enforcement
Daily cap enforced only in src/stores/scanStore.ts (client-side Zustand) - bypassed by any direct HTTP call
findings.businessImpact: Any unauthenticated caller can POST arbitrary barcodes and trigger paid Gemini Flash, GPT-5-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Firecrawl calls without limit. At the observed throughput an attacker can exhaust daily API budgets in seconds.
findings.securityImpact: Unauthenticated access to a paid AI pipeline. Daily spend cap exists only in client JavaScript and is trivially bypassed. No 429 was observed across 3,318 requests.
findings.explanation: The POST handler at /api/ai-lookup reads no auth token, cookie, or session. There is no middleware protecting /api routes. The server returns the daily limit value only in the GET config response for the client to read; the POST handler never checks whether that limit has been reached. Any process that can reach localhost:3000 (or a deployed equivalent) can drain AI spend at will.
findings.fix: 1. Add server-side authentication (Firebase Admin verifyIdToken or equivalent) to the POST handler as the first check. 2. Implement server-side rate limiting (e.g. Upstash Redis or an in-memory sliding window for single-instance) keyed to user+IP. 3. Enforce the daily spend cap server-side, persisted across processes (Redis or Firestore counter), not in client state. 4. Return HTTP 429 when the cap or rate limit is exceeded.

findings.title: GET /api/ai-lookup exposes full AI stack fingerprint to unauthenticated callers
findings.affects: any unauthenticated internet-facing user once deployed
evidence: No auth header required; 200 returned on all 20 sequential requests and all 3,318 flood requests
findings.businessImpact: Reveals which AI providers are configured, their model names, daily cap, whether open-web fallback is active, and whether the app is running in mock mode. This gives an attacker a precise map of what providers to abuse and what the spend ceiling is.
findings.securityImpact: Information disclosure. Combined with the unauthenticated POST, an attacker knows exactly which model to target and that no cap is enforced server-side.
findings.explanation: The GET handler is intentionally unauthenticated to let the client self-configure. This is reasonable in a single-user local app but becomes a recon endpoint once the app is deployed or exposed on a network.
findings.fix: Gate the GET handler behind the same auth check as POST, or strip the model names and limit value from the public response, returning only the minimum booleans the client needs to decide whether to attempt a decode.

findings.title: Client-side-only daily AI spend cap is trivially bypassed by direct HTTP calls
findings.affects: owner's Gemini, OpenAI, Firecrawl API budgets
evidence: src/stores/scanStore.ts lines 1061-1067: dailyCount computed in Zustand client store from settings.lastResetDate / settings.dailyLookupCount
src/stores/circuitBreaker.ts: isDailyCapReached check runs client-side only
src/app/api/ai-lookup/route.ts: grep for dailyCount/dailyLimit returns only the GET payload line (187); no check in POST handler
findings.businessImpact: An attacker who POSTs directly to /api/ai-lookup bypasses the daily cap entirely and can trigger unlimited paid AI calls regardless of the configured limit.
findings.securityImpact: Defense in depth failure: the only spend guard is in untrusted client code.
findings.explanation: The daily lookup limit (default 200, configurable via AI_LOOKUP_DAILY_LIMIT) is tracked in Zustand localStorage state on the browser. The server route reads the limit value only to return it in the GET config; it never enforces it. A curl loop or script hitting POST directly ignores the cap completely.
findings.fix: Move the daily cap counter to server-side persistent storage (Redis, Firestore, or a server memory store for single-instance). Check and decrement it atomically in the POST handler before calling any provider. Return 429 when exceeded.

findings.title: Playwright config spreads full OS process environment into test report, capturing any shell secret
findings.affects: any developer whose shell has secrets set (CI runners, dev machines)
evidence: reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json line 77: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY captured from shell env
reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json line 160: SERPAPI_KEY captured from shell env
reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json is not in .gitignore (only /test-results and /playwright-report are excluded)
findings.businessImpact: Every time qa:bots runs, any shell secret (API keys, tokens, credentials) present in the developer or CI environment is serialized into the committed report file. This is a persistent, silent credential exfiltration path that grows with every test run.
findings.securityImpact: Systematic secret leakage pattern. Will recur on every qa:bots invocation until fixed.
findings.explanation: The spread of ...process.env is the pattern error. The Playwright JSON reporter records the full webServer config including its env block. The report file is git-tracked and committed repeatedly. Any new shell variable present at qa:bots time will be committed.
findings.fix: Replace '...process.env' with an explicit allowlist: only pass the specific env vars the Next.js server needs (IS_E2E, NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_AUTH_BYPASS, GEMINI_API_KEY if required for specific e2e tests, etc.). Add 'reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json' and 'reports/human-bots/latest/cloud-playwright-results.json' to .gitignore. Add a gitleaks pre-commit hook.

findings.title: undici high-severity CVEs (TLS bypass, HTTP header injection, DoS, response queue poisoning)
findings.affects: server-side HTTP fetching (page fetch, AI provider calls, Firecrawl)
evidence: npm audit: undici 7.0.0 - 7.27.2 has 7 CVEs: GHSA-vmh5-mc38-953g (TLS cert bypass, high), GHSA-p88m-4jfj-68fv (HTTP header injection), GHSA-vxpw-j846-p89q (WebSocket DoS), GHSA-hm92-r4w5-c3mj (cross-origin SOCKS5 reuse), GHSA-35p6-xmwp-9g52 (response queue poisoning), GHSA-g8m3-5g58-fq7m (SameSite downgrade), GHSA-pr7r-676h-xcf6 (cross-user cache disclosure)
npm audit fix available without breaking change
findings.businessImpact: Server-side fetching of barcode/product pages and AI provider calls use Node's http stack which depends on undici. TLS bypass and response queue poisoning are the most critical in a context where the app fetches untrusted vendor URLs.
findings.securityImpact: TLS certificate validation bypass (CVSS 7.4) allows MITM on outbound HTTPS requests. HTTP header injection and response queue poisoning enable cross-request data corruption. Cross-user cache disclosure risks leaking one user's product lookup to another.
findings.explanation: undici is a transitive dependency via Next.js. Seven CVEs exist in the installed version range. Most are fixable with 'npm audit fix' without breaking changes.
findings.fix: Run 'npm audit fix' to update undici. Verify no regressions in page-fetch and AI provider integration tests after update.

findings.title: keySafety test does not cover FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, SERPAPI_KEY, or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY client-side reads
findings.affects: future developers adding client-side Firecrawl or SerpAPI integrations
evidence: src/services/keySafety.test.ts FORBIDDEN list covers: GEMINI_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, Firebase Admin patterns only
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY, SERPAPI_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY not in FORBIDDEN list
FIRECRAWL_API_KEY is actively used server-side (route.ts line 243)
findings.businessImpact: A developer could add FIRECRAWL_API_KEY to a client component and the existing guard would not catch it.
findings.securityImpact: Gap in automated key-safety enforcement. Low immediate risk (no client-side read found currently) but the guard should be complete.
findings.explanation: The keySafety test is a valuable control but it only lists two AI provider keys. As new providers are added (Firecrawl, SerpAPI), their keys should be added to the FORBIDDEN list to prevent accidental client-side exposure.
findings.fix: Add 'process.env.FIRECRAWL_API_KEY', 'process.env.SERPAPI_KEY', and any other server-only keys to the FORBIDDEN list in src/services/keySafety.test.ts.

findings.title: SSRF hostname guard is DNS-resolution-blind (hostname-only, no post-resolution IP check)
findings.affects: server-side page fetch and Firecrawl discovery paths
evidence: src/services/ai/urlSafety.ts comment line 3: 'NOTE: this is a hostname/IP-literal guard, not full DNS-resolution check'
Only checks literal hostname and IP-literal strings; a DNS rebinding or custom DNS name resolving to 169.254.169.254 or 10.x would pass
findings.businessImpact: An attacker who controls a DNS name (via a poisoned AI response or barcode vendor page) that resolves to an internal IP could trigger SSRF against cloud metadata services or internal hosts.
findings.securityImpact: DNS rebinding SSRF bypass. Confidence is medium because exploitation requires controlling DNS resolution, which is harder in practice.
findings.explanation: The urlSafety guard correctly blocks literal private IPs and known internal hostnames. The acknowledged limitation is that it does not resolve the hostname and re-check the resulting IP. In cloud environments (AWS, GCP) the metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254 is reachable from any internal process, and a crafted domain resolving to that IP would pass the guard.
findings.fix: After the hostname check, resolve the hostname to its IP(s) and run isPrivateIp() on each resolved address before allowing the fetch. Use a short DNS timeout. This eliminates DNS rebinding as an attack vector.

findings.title: Session controls (name field, location dropdown, 3 buttons) are always expanded above the feed
findings.recommendation: defer / hide-until-needed: collapse session controls behind the existing 'More options' toggle by default; show only the session name badge and a single 'Manage session' link at rest; the scanner loop never needs to touch session controls mid-count

findings.title: Export dropdown and Import button sit inside the active scan panel, adding choices during the repetitive scan loop
findings.recommendation: defer: move Export and Import to the session controls collapse or to a post-session summary step; they are end-of-session actions, not per-scan actions

findings.title: 'Try saving again' button is always rendered in the sync row even when online and all items are synced
findings.recommendation: hide-until-needed: only surface the retry button when syncStatus is 'pending' or a sync failure exists; remove it entirely from the happy path

findings.title: Delete button in 'Your counts' rows is the same visual weight as Modify with no confirmation step visible
findings.recommendation: group / default: render Modify as the primary action; move Delete behind a row overflow menu or add an inline confirmation step so a misclick during fast scanning does not silently erase a counted row

findings.title: Scan feed table has 7 columns (Time, Barcode, Product, Part number, Qty after, Status, Reason, Saved) -- the Reason column requires reading mid-scan
findings.recommendation: group / progressive-disclosure: collapse Barcode and Reason into an expandable row detail; show only Product, Qty after, and Status in the default feed view; full detail available on row tap/click

findings.title: On mobile the session + sync + export block consumes most of the viewport before the scan feed, pushing the live feedback area below the fold
findings.recommendation: hide-until-needed: on mobile collapse the session block to a single status line by default; the scan input and live feed must be the first content a user sees without scrolling

findings.title: Products page is a flat unsorted table with no search, filter, or sort controls; at scale locating a product requires scanning the full list
findings.recommendation: defer: add a single search-by-name input as the only visible control; category filter and sort can live behind an 'Advanced' toggle to keep the default view calm

findings.title: Settings page exposes internal AI provider names (Gemini, OpenAI) to shop operators
findings.recommendation: Replace provider-specific labels with product-level language ('Smart Lookup: On/Off', 'Cloud identification enabled'). Internal provider routing is an implementation detail that should not reach the operator UI.

findings.title: Products page has no search, filter, or sort on a multi-category catalog
findings.recommendation: Add a search-by-name/brand/category input and sortable column headers to the Products table. A prospect with 200 SKUs will immediately notice this gap during a demo.

findings.title: 'Saved: 0' while rows show 'Synced' looks like a bug to a prospect evaluating reliability
findings.recommendation: Fix the Saved counter to reflect actual synced state or remove it. A data reliability signal that contradicts row-level badges destroys trust in a sales demo.

findings.title: Role-gated server-side resolution and data protection (customer browsers never download the alias/catalog DB)
evidence: performance_smoke.md: 'today the local store includes the alias/catalog DB - a correctness + security concern flagged by SecurityLeakBot'
HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md: full role model, server-side customer resolution endpoint, role-aware serializers all deferred
export_headers_by_role.json: role gating not yet implemented (auth-bypass only)
findings.businessImpact: Without this the app cannot be sold to a second shop: every employee browser downloads the full global alias and catalog database, leaking competitor product mappings and making multi-tenant billing impossible. Shipping this converts a single-owner demo into a sellable SaaS product.
findings.explanation: The current app ships the entire alias/catalog/index DB to every browser session via Zustand/localStorage regardless of role. A counter employee or viewer sees - and can extract - the same internal raw-code database that the platform owner uses. HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md already has the full design: server-side resolution endpoint returns only product-facing fields to customer roles; platformOwner retains full local access; Firestore rules + role-aware serializers enforce the boundary. Role model: platformOwner (full DB) vs businessOwner/admin (operational, no raw-code export) vs counter/viewer (product-facing only). Offline customers queue their own scans and resolve on reconnect - they never receive the bulk catalog.
findings.fix: Implement server-side customer resolution endpoint (POST /api/resolve) that accepts a scanned code and returns only product-facing fields (name, brand, part number, specs, category, match status). Wire Firestore rules to block customer-role clients from reading alias/catalog collections directly. Add role-aware serializers for UI components, CSV export, and API responses. Enforce platformOwner as a platform-level permission (not a localStorage flag). Move the alias/catalog index off the customer client store.

findings.title: Per-user scan attribution (who scanned what, when, in each session)
evidence: manager_insights.md: '[important soon] Who scanned what (per-user attribution in the feed)'
security/01-scan.png: every feed row shows the same single 'N' avatar with no user label
mobile-scan.png: scan feed has no user column
findings.businessImpact: A shop running 2-3 counters simultaneously during a physical inventory cannot identify which employee miscounted a row. Resolving a discrepancy currently requires re-counting the whole section. Per-user attribution cuts discrepancy investigation from hours to minutes and is the #1 ask from any multi-employee shop.
findings.explanation: Every ScanEvent already has a userId field in types.ts and the Firebase auth model assigns each counter a UID, but the scan feed UI never displays user identity - it shows a single avatar initial. The manager has no way to filter, sort, or audit by counter. This is a core manager feature for any shop with more than one person scanning.
findings.fix: Add userId + displayName to each ScanEvent at scan time (already available from Firebase Auth). Show a user badge on each feed row. Add a 'Filter by user' dropdown to the feed. Include the user column in CSV exports (manager-role export only, stripped from counter/viewer exports). Add a manager-facing per-user summary to the finished-session view.

findings.title: Session history list with comparison (view and export any past inventory count)
evidence: mobile-scan.png: session UI shows only 'Default Session' with no history link
exports.png: export menu shows only the current session's counts - no historical export
findings.businessImpact: A shop that counts inventory weekly cannot compare this week's count to last week's without re-exporting and manually diffing spreadsheets. Session history with a delta view is the feature that turns a one-time tool into a recurring workflow - and the anchor for a paid subscription (pay per month, not per use).
findings.explanation: When a session is finished via 'Finish session', its data is effectively lost from the UI. There is no session list, no way to reopen a past session's export, and no diff view. The Firebase data model already scopes events by session_id, so the raw data exists. The missing pieces are a sessions index page, a per-session detail/export view, and an optional side-by-side delta column showing gain/loss vs a previous session.
findings.fix: Add a Sessions page (or expandable section in the manager view) listing finished sessions with date, item count, and user. Each session row links to a read-only count detail and a CSV/XLSX export. Add a 'Compare to previous session' toggle that shows a +/- delta column. Gate the detail view to manager/owner roles.

findings.title: Product search and filter on the Products page
evidence: manager_insights.md: '[important soon] Product search / filter on Products page'
manager.png: Products page shows 5 rows in a flat unfiltered table with no search input
findings.businessImpact: A real shop has 50 to 5000 products. Without search, the Products page is unusable beyond the demo data. Every onboarding call where the owner uploads their catalog and then cannot find a product is a lost deal or a support ticket.
findings.explanation: The current Products page (screenshot: manager.png) is a bare table with Name, Brand, Category, Specs, Part number, Image, and Location columns and no search box, category filter, or sort controls. A shop with hundreds of tires grouped by brand and size needs to type a brand name or a size spec and see matching rows instantly. This is table-stakes for any product management page.
findings.fix: Add a search input above the Products table that filters by name, brand, part number, or specs (client-side filter on the loaded set; add server-side pagination when the catalog exceeds ~500 rows). Add a category dropdown filter. Add clickable column headers for sort. Small build, high daily use.

findings.title: Low-stock alerts and reorder point memory per product
evidence: manager_insights.md: '[paid add-on candidate] Low-stock / overstock & stock-target memory'
manager.png: Products table has no min/max/target quantity columns
exports.png: Final count table shows current qty with no threshold indicator
findings.businessImpact: A tire shop or auto parts counter that sets minimum stock levels and gets an alert the moment a count session shows a product below par avoids stockouts and emergency orders. This is the feature shop owners describe when they say 'I want smart inventory' - and it justifies a paid tier above the base plan.
findings.explanation: The products data model has no min_qty / max_qty / reorder_point fields today. After a count session the manager has to manually scan the export looking for low rows. Adding a threshold per product and a post-session alert (red badge on low rows in the counts table, a summary email or in-app notification, and a filtered 'Low stock' export) converts the app from a counting tool into an active inventory management tool.
findings.fix: Add min_qty and reorder_point fields to the Product model (optional, default null). Add an inline edit control on the Products page to set thresholds. After a session finishes, compare final counts to thresholds and show a 'Low stock' badge on matching rows in the count table. Add a one-click 'Export low stock only' CSV. Gate threshold editing to owner/manager role.

findings.title: Audit history viewer (surface the already-written audit log in the UI)
evidence: manager_insights.md: '[important soon] Audit history viewer (audit is written; no UI)'
HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md: audit events listed (alias_link_warning_shown, alias_link_override, alias_moved_or_unlinked, global_alias_candidate_created)
findings.businessImpact: When a product miscounts or an alias is linked incorrectly the manager today has zero visibility into what happened or who did it. An audit viewer lets them answer 'why does this barcode now point to a different product?' in 30 seconds instead of a support call. This is also a compliance requirement for some regulated product categories (medical supplies, controlled parts).
findings.explanation: The Firebase data model already writes audit events for alias approvals, overrides, and count modifications, but there is no UI page to browse them. The manager_insights report explicitly called this out as 'important soon'. The data exists - the feature is a read-only paginated list with filters by event type, user, and date range.
findings.fix: Add an Audit Log page (manager/owner role only) with a paginated table: timestamp, user, event type, affected product/alias, before/after values, and session context. Add filters by event type and date range. Add CSV export of the audit log. No new data model changes needed - the events are already written.

findings.title: In-row quantity correction button on the counts table
evidence: reports/human-bots/latest/playwright-results.json: CustomerReadableControlsBot FAILED - getByRole('button', { name: 'Correct' }).first() not found in final-count-body
exports.png: counts table shows Modify/Delete actions but no Correct/adjust-quantity affordance visible to customer role
findings.businessImpact: A counter who scans a product 5 times but meant 4 currently has to delete the row and rescan or use the Modify flow, which is a multi-step detour that interrupts scanning momentum. An inline +/- quantity adjuster on each count row reduces correction time from 10-15 seconds to 2 seconds and eliminates miscounts caused by clumsy workarounds.
findings.explanation: The bot test expected a 'Correct' button inside the final-count-body that was not found. The existing UI shows Modify and Delete (exports.png) but these are not touch-sized affordances for a fast in-session correction. A +1 / -1 or direct numeric input on the counts row, accessible to the counter role, is the missing piece. The Modify flow may exist but is not reachable by the expected selector, which means the customer/counter role view likely lacks it.
findings.fix: Add a visible quantity adjust control (+/-  or editable number field) to each row in the FinalCountTable that is accessible to counter and viewer roles. Ensure the control meets the 44px minimum touch target. Label it clearly (e.g. 'Adjust qty'). Wire it to the existing store increment/decrement logic with an audit event. Fix the test selector to match the new label.

findings.title: Part-number-only CSV import with enrichment (onboard an existing product list that has no barcodes yet)
evidence: manager_insights.md: '[paid add-on candidate (deferred)] Part-number-only CSV import + enrichment'
HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md: import as candidate/local product with missing_barcode status, queue enrichment to find UPC/EAN/GTIN
mobile-scan.png: Import button shows only 'Products CSV' with no guidance on format or partial-barcode handling
findings.businessImpact: Every existing shop has a spreadsheet of part numbers or SKUs. If the onboarding step is 'paste your CSV and we will find the barcodes', the shop can start scanning the same day without manually looking up every UPC. This removes the single biggest friction point in converting a free trial to a paid account.
findings.explanation: Today a shop owner who has 500 tires in a spreadsheet (part numbers, no EAN/UPC) cannot import them into the app meaningfully - the import expects a full product definition. The deferred plan in HOTFIX_FOLLOWUPS.md is clear: import rows become local candidate products with missing_barcode status; part number / SKU is saved as a businessLocalAlias; enrichment queues an AI/catalog lookup to find the UPC/EAN/GTIN. The shop can then scan a physical barcode and the system proposes the match for one-click approval.
findings.fix: Extend the Products CSV import to accept rows with only part_number / sku (no barcode required). Each imported row creates a local product record with status=missing_barcode. Queue an async enrichment job per row (use existing AI decode pipeline with part-number prompt). When a physical barcode is scanned and matches an enriched candidate, show a one-click 'Is this [product name]?' prompt. Mark confirmed matches as approved aliases.

findings.title: Mobile scan input auto-focus on page load (eliminate the required tap before scanning on phones)
evidence: ux_scorecard.md: 'Find where to scan' FAIL - friction 1 - 'scan input is the focused default' but the bot still failed to find it
top_ux_confusions.md: '[P2] Find where to scan - scan input is the focused default'
mobile-scan.png: scan input shows placeholder text 'Click here, then scan or type a code' - the word 'Click' signals a required manual tap
findings.businessImpact: A counter using a Bluetooth barcode scanner on a phone must tap the scan box after every navigation or page reload. In a busy shop doing 200 scans per hour this adds 200 extra taps per session. Removing the required tap saves roughly 3-4 minutes per hour of active scanning and eliminates the most common new-user support question.
findings.explanation: The scan input placeholder says 'Click here, then scan or type a code' which is accurate - on mobile the browser security model prevents auto-focus without a prior user gesture. The fix is two-part: (1) change the placeholder copy to 'Tap here, then scan' to set correct expectation; (2) add a prominent 'Tap to start scanning' banner that auto-dismisses after the first tap and sets focus, so new users never miss where to start. The underlying auto-focus-after-submit logic already works correctly; only the initial page-load focus needs the tap affordance improvement.
findings.fix: Add a visible 'Tap to start scanning' call-to-action banner above the scan input on mobile viewports when the input is not yet focused. Auto-dismiss on first tap/focus. Update placeholder copy to 'Tap here, then scan or type a code'. Add a data-testid so the bot can confirm the affordance is present. Consider a 'Request persistent wake-lock' option for phone-mounted scanner setups.

findings.title: Tekmetric Tire Suite is the single biggest threat: embedded + incremental cost
findings.businessImpact: A shop already paying $179-$409/month for Tekmetric shop management can add Tire Suite for $39/month -- a small incremental spend on a platform they already trust. Smart Inventory must justify a separate product purchase to that same shop owner.
findings.explanation: Tekmetric bundles tire quoting, TireConnect, and parts inventory inside the RO workflow. A tire shop owner who is already on Tekmetric has almost no reason to add a standalone inventory counter unless Smart Inventory offers something Tekmetric cannot: a fast offline-tolerant standalone count session with AI decode for unknown codes and no RO required.
findings.fix: Position Smart Inventory explicitly as the count-cycle layer that works beside (not against) Tekmetric. Highlight offline tolerance, 75 ms scan speed, and the idempotent no-double-count guarantee as complementary to an RO platform, not a replacement. Build a CSV export format that imports cleanly into Tekmetric.

findings.title: Export gap: only final-counts CSV is wired; products, aliases, raw log, and unknowns exports are missing
findings.businessImpact: Every competitor (Sortly, inFlow, Lightspeed) offers multi-format exports including raw transaction logs and product lists. A shop evaluating Smart Inventory will ask 'how do I get my data out?' and the answer is currently only one CSV type. This is a sales blocker for shops that need audit trails or want to feed data into accounting software.
findings.explanation: The export bot confirmed that only the 'final counts' CSV button is present. Products, aliases, raw scan log, and unknowns all show '(button not present)' or '(no download)'. Competitors use rich export as a proof point for data ownership and accountant handoff.
findings.fix: Wire the four missing export buttons. Priority order: (1) raw scan log (audit trail), (2) unknowns (helps the shop resolve backlog), (3) products, (4) aliases. Each adds a credible 'your data is yours' story that competes with Sortly and inFlow.

findings.title: Role gating not yet live: all users see all exports and all data
findings.businessImpact: Sortly, inFlow, and Lightspeed all use tiered user roles (view-only, counter, manager, owner) as an upgrade lever and a security selling point. Without role gating, Smart Inventory cannot be sold to a shop owner who has employees and does not want technicians exporting the full product database or modifying counts.
findings.explanation: The export bot records role as 'current (auth-bypass; role gating not yet implemented)'. This is a known deferred feature but it blocks the multi-user shop scenario that every mid-size competitor addresses.
findings.fix: Implement at minimum a two-role model (scanner vs. manager) before the next sales conversation with a multi-employee shop. Scanner role: scan, view own feed. Manager role: full export, Needs Review resolution, settings.

findings.title: Needs Review copy is unclear to a first-time shop user -- a UX gap vs. every polished competitor
findings.businessImpact: When a shop owner demo-scans an unknown barcode, the Needs Review page is the first thing they interact with that is not immediate feedback. If the copy is confusing, they assume the product is broken. Sortly and Square polish their unknown-item flows heavily because that is often where a trial user forms their opinion.
findings.explanation: The UX bot gave 'Understand Needs Review' a friction score of 3/5 and flagged it as a quick fix. Internal terms like 'AI lookup' and provider names appear in Settings, which exposes implementation details rather than shop-friendly language.
findings.fix: Rename 'Needs Review' to 'Unrecognized Items' or 'Items to Identify' in all user-facing copy. Replace 'AI lookup' with 'Auto-identify'. Strip provider names from Settings UI. This is a quick fix per the bot scorecard.

findings.title: No preloaded catalog: Smart Inventory requires manual seeding or scan-and-resolve before any item is 'Known'
findings.businessImpact: Lightspeed ships an 8-million-item preloaded catalog. Sortly supports bulk CSV import. A new shop owner evaluating Smart Inventory faces a cold-start problem: the first scan of every product is Unknown until the AI decode fires or a human resolves it. Competitors let a shop import its existing product list and be operational in hours.
findings.explanation: Smart Inventory's resolver returns Known only from approved aliases or verified products. There is no bulk-import flow for a shop's existing product list visible in the bot reports or export structure. The tire corpus (tire_corpus_flat.csv) exists but is not surfaced as a user-facing catalog seed.
findings.fix: Expose a CSV import for the products table (name, brand, category, part numbers as aliases). Pre-populate the tire corpus as a known-alias seed so any shop scanning standard tire part numbers gets instant Known matches from day one. This directly addresses the cold-start objection in a sales demo.

findings.title: No purchase-order or reorder workflow: Smart Inventory is count-only vs. full inventory lifecycle competitors
findings.businessImpact: inFlow, Sortly Plus, Lightspeed, and Square Plus all include purchase orders and reorder-point alerts. A shop owner who counts stock expects the software to also tell them what to reorder and help them place the order. Without this, Smart Inventory is only the first step of the workflow.
findings.explanation: The current feature set covers scan-to-count and export. There is no reorder threshold, low-stock alert, or vendor/PO module visible in any bot report or the codebase CLAUDE.md feature list.
findings.fix: Add low-stock alert thresholds as a near-term feature (set par level per product; flag when count drops below). Full PO generation can be a later phase. Even a simple 'flag for reorder' column in the final-counts CSV makes the tool more complete vs. Sortly.

findings.title: Locale-specific catalog growth (localStorage) will degrade performance and expose catalog to the client
findings.businessImpact: The performance bot flagged that the local store currently includes the alias/catalog DB and notes that localStorage will grow as the catalog grows. Competitors (Lightspeed, inFlow) use server-side catalog lookups. If a demo shop has a large tire catalog, the localStorage approach will hit browser limits and expose the catalog on the client -- a security and scalability concern that will surface in any technical due-diligence conversation.
findings.explanation: Current localStorage size is 4660 bytes (well under limit for now), but the bot explicitly flagged this as a reason that deferred server-side customer resolution matters. The catalog/alias DB living in localStorage is both a size risk and a data-exposure risk (SecurityLeakBot concern noted in the same report).
findings.fix: Move catalog/alias resolution to server-side lookup before the catalog exceeds a few hundred items. This is already flagged as a deferred item in the performance bot note. Prioritize before a larger-catalog demo or multi-user pilot.

scores.reason: Two blocker-class security holes (committed live keys, unauthenticated paid AI endpoint) plus a mobile blocker mean this is a strong single-user demo but not deployable or sellable yet.
scores.topFix: Rotate keys, gate /api/ai-lookup server-side, fix mobile scan layout.

scores.reason: Desktop reads clearly in under 10 seconds, but the 'Saved: 0 while rows say Synced' counter looks like a bug, provider-name jargon leaks, and Products page has no search at scale.
scores.topFix: Fix the Saved counter contradiction and strip internal AI/provider jargon from all user-facing screens.

scores.reason: Live API keys committed to git history (three commits), unauthenticated POST to a paid AI pipeline, client-side-only spend cap, undici CVEs, and DNS-blind SSRF guard.
scores.topFix: Rotate exposed keys, scrub git history, add server-side auth + rate limit + spend cap on /api/ai-lookup.

scores.reason: Role gating is UI-only; the full alias/catalog DB and raw codes sit in the Zustand store and global catalogEntries is readable by any signed-in user, so devtools or direct Firestore reads expose everything.
scores.topFix: Implement the deferred server-side customer resolution endpoint so customer browsers never receive raw codes or the catalog DB.

scores.reason: businessId is taken from the request body; the membership check exists but the no-Firebase/emulator fallback is unaudited and there is no integration test proving cross-tenant access is blocked. NEXT_PUBLIC_OPEN_ACCESS can bypass the whole auth guard.
scores.topFix: Validate authenticated uid against requested businessId server-side and add a cross-tenant denial integration test.

scores.reason: Session/export/import controls bury scan feedback below the fold at 390px, the feed table truncates Status and Saved columns, and the scan box is not auto-focused on load.
scores.topFix: Collapse session controls into one row and put the scan input plus last-scan confirmation first on mobile.

scores.reason: Auto-focus-after-submit works and friction is low, but the input is not focused on initial load, the placeholder says 'Click here' which misleads, and a same-weight unconfirmed Delete sits next to Modify in count rows.
scores.topFix: Auto-focus on page load, fix placeholder copy, and demote/confirm the Delete action.

scores.reason: No correctness defects were surfaced in this finding set; the Gemini-first then ChatGPT pipeline with app-side evidence verification is the documented design. Lower than full only due to lack of fresh accuracy proof in these reports.
scores.topFix: Add a current decode accuracy proof run to confirm the master baseline still holds.

scores.reason: Internal fields (verifiedFacts, guesses, confidence, autoVerifyScore) leak to customer roles, the name is jargon-heavy, and a missing 'Correct' button suggests the in-row correction path may be absent or renamed.
scores.topFix: Wrap internal AI fields in the isPlatform guard and rename 'Needs Review' to plain language like 'Unrecognized items'.

scores.reason: The daily spend cap lives only in client Zustand state; a direct HTTP POST bypasses it entirely, the endpoint is unauthenticated, and a flood test ran 3,318 requests with zero 429s.
scores.topFix: Enforce the daily cap and rate limit server-side with a persistent counter and return 429 when exceeded.

scores.reason: Offline-tolerant scan, pending sync queue, retry, and idempotency are documented and built; the only related concern is the always-visible 'Try saving again' button on the happy path. No offline defects surfaced.
scores.topFix: Hide the retry button unless a sync is actually pending or failed.

scores.reason: Only the final-counts CSV is wired; products, aliases, raw scan log, and unknowns exports are absent, there is no bulk product import or part-number-only onboarding, and export role gating is not live.
scores.topFix: Wire the missing exports (raw log, unknowns, products, aliases) and add a products CSV import for cold-start onboarding.

scores.reason: Strong core (fast idempotent offline count with AI decode) but missing the features that make it a recurring paid product: per-user attribution, session history/compare, product search, low-stock alerts, and an audit viewer.
scores.topFix: Ship product search and session history first; they convert a one-time tool into a recurring subscription workflow.

scores.reason: No pricing model was tested in these findings; confidence is dragged down by the lack of role tiers, missing exports, and cold-start problem that all weaken what can be charged for today.
scores.topFix: Lock the role model and recurring features (session history, low-stock) so a clear paid tier exists to price.

scores.reason: Per the provided signal: Tekmetric Tire Suite adds tire inventory for $39/month on a platform shops already trust, and Sortly/inFlow/Lightspeed beat us on preloaded catalogs, multi-format export, role tiers, and PO/reorder workflows.
scores.topFix: Position as the offline-tolerant count layer that exports cleanly into Tekmetric, and close the catalog-import and export gaps.

scores.reason: Audit events are written but have no UI viewer, there is no per-user attribution to investigate discrepancies, no .env.example for onboarding, and jargon-heavy copy drives support questions.
scores.topFix: Surface the existing audit log in a manager-only viewer and add per-user scan attribution.
